change.description: Add provider-call AI usage metering across assistant-facing clipping, search, indexing, tags, icons, and model validation paths, with contained token dimensions, retry-aware settlement, rolling personal quota helpers, additive daily result counts, daily rollups, detail retention, and an existing-scheduler maintenance job.

planned.reasoning: The implementation preserves existing provider and public response contracts, adds operational accounting and quota enforcement helpers, and extends the daily usage summary with additive result-count columns through a forward-only migration.

evidence.command: Defines separate personal quota and sitewide provider usage scope, retry semantics, containment, estimates, and retention
Locks rolling token/question windows, three conversations, reset behavior, provider dimensions, and 90-day detail retention

current.reasoning: The candidate records every attempted provider call, preserves user/feature/provider/model/status/raw dimensions without prompt or answer bodies, observes raw provider usage before SDK normalization, uses conservative reservations with in-place corrections, and keeps automatic retries from adding question counts while manual retries remain separate. Late settlements trigger an idempotent backfill of already-existing affected summaries, with the complete detail read and summary write serialized in one immediate transaction. runAiUsageMaintenance remains the sole maintenance entry point, defaults scheduled maintenance to Asia/Shanghai, and is registered as the daily ai-usage-maintenance job in the existing scheduler. The production console is the sole scheduler owner and stops that worker in its existing shutdown path; the development-only gateway does not start a second worker. Daily summaries now preserve success, failure, and cancellation counts across detail cleanup. Upstream model catalog metadata discovery remains outside model-validation metering; actual admin validation calls carry the authenticated backend identity context. Assistant content-search/search user metering context remains T4-owned and is intentionally not changed here.
